transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-22 09:30 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Michael Turner (Aurum VP Procurement), Laura Chen (Aurum CISO), Jamal Rivera (Aurum Head of MLOps), Priya Shah (Aurum Legal)

Summary (auto): Procurement + legal kickoff covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing approval path and onboarding tasks. Some transcription errors present; names/acronyms occasionally mis-labeled.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, Samira here from Redwood, thanks for joining. Quick roll call then we'll jump in.
[00:12] Michael: Hey Samira, Michael here.
[00:14] Laura: Laura Chen, CISO.
[00:16] Jamal: Jamal Rivera, MLOps.
[00:18] Priya: Priya Shah, legal.
[00:20] Ethan: Ethan Ross, solutions eng from Redwood.
[00:22] Samira: Great, thanks. Goal today is to run through the MSA/DPA redlines you sent, confirm any SLA expectations and pricing approval timelines, and give you the onboarding artifacts Ethan mentioned. Sound right?
[00:32] Michael: Yep that's right. Procurement wants to get a clear path to PO — our finance folks need a final price + contract terms. We're also flagging data residency and KMS integration as blockers for approval right now.
[00:45] Priya: On the legal side: we submitted a few DPA redlines—mostly around subprocessors, data retention, and audit rights. Also want SOC2 attestation and a clearer breach notification timeline.
[00:58] Laura: And security needs to validate the KMS/HSM flow, whether Redwood stores keys, or we manage keys in our cloud KMS. We prefer customer-managed KMS.
[01:12] Ethan: Understood — Redwood supports customer KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for private deployments; for hosted there's a managed KMS we can use but we do offer a bring-your-own-key option for enterprise. I'll share the integration notes.
[01:27] Jamal: Quick technical: latency is a concern for real-time inference. If we go private on-prem vs dedicated cloud, what's the delta in cost and SLOs?
[01:40] Ethan: Usually hosted has best time-to-value but less isolation. Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and dedicated GPUs — lower variance in latency. Private/VPC/on-prem gives the most control but higher ops overhead and cost. For our 100ms P95 SLO target, a dedicated config with optimized kernels can hit that at XX hardware — sorry that's a bit vague over the call but we have benchmark data.
[02:05] Michael: Can we get the benchmark spreadsheet? Finance will want unit economics.
[02:10] Samira: Yes, I'll attach the pricing spreadsheet and Ethan will send the benchmark sheet.
[02:15] Priya: Back to DPA: we flagged subprocessors list — need confirmation of any cloud provider or third-party labs that will see data.
[02:28] Ethan: We use cloud infra partners and occasionally third-party logging for ops; the subprocessors list is in the SOC/security pack. We'll share an updated list and can mark anything as restricted if you need.
[02:42] Laura: Also, SSO — we need SAML/OIDC SSO with SCIM provisioning and role-based access control. Can Redwood integrate with our Okta?
[02:55] Samira: Yes, SAML and SCIM are supported; RBAC is configurable. Ethan, I'll let you confirm the exact SCIM attributes we support.
[03:05] Ethan: We'll send an Okta integration guide; in private deployments there's direct enterprise SSO integration.
[03:12] Speaker 1: (mumble)
[03:15] Priya: On liability caps — your MSA has a standard cap at fees paid in 12 months. Our legal team is pushing for a higher cap or carve-outs for data breaches.
[03:26] Samira: I hear that — typical trajectory is to table that with legal teams, we can surface where we can be flexible. We'll provide suggested language.
[03:34] Michael: Timeline: procurement wants to sign off within two weeks if we can get final redlines and pricing. Is that feasible?
[03:41] Samira: Sounds doable. We'll aim to get redlined MSA/DPA back in 48–72 hours.
[03:48] Jamal: For onboarding — what's the expected runbook? Who from our team needs to be involved?
[03:55] Ethan: Onboarding runbook typically includes: account setup, SSO and RBAC, KMS integration, model pinning and test workloads, performance bench, and a canary rollout. We recommend 2–3 SRE/MLops folks for the initial week. We'll share a checklist.
[04:18] Michael: Great. Any concerns about data residency — we operate in EU and US, we need data stored in-region.
[04:24] Ethan: We support region routing and data residency options; for hosted accounts we can pin region and for private deploy we deploy in your VPC/region.
[04:33] Priya: Can you reconfirm breach notification SLA — current DPA asks for 72 hours; we want 48.
[04:39] Samira: I'll flag to legal — we'll check the standard is 72 but we can discuss 48 for critical incidents.
[04:47] Laura: Also need audit logs and retention. What's the default retention?
[04:52] Ethan: Default is 90 days in hosted, but we offer extended retention as an add-on. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[05:01] Michael: About pricing — our procurement team needs a clear per-token/per-embedding pricing and a committed reserved capacity option. We're evaluating between pay-as-you-go hosted and a 3-month dedicated commit.
[05:14] Samira: We have both. I'll include price tiers for hosted and a recommended dedicated configuration with committed monthly throughput and potential discounts.
[05:25] Jamal: Can you also include quantization/accuracy tradeoffs in the benchmark? We need to know cost vs quality.
[05:31] Ethan: Yes, the benchmark spreadsheet will include quantization profiles and quality regression notes tied to our eval prompts.
[05:37] Priya: Need to know subprocessors and whether Redwood will push model updates that could change outputs — we want stability and change control.
[05:46] Samira: We have model version pinning and rollout policies; we'll describe the change control process in the onboarding docs.
[05:55] Michael: On PO — finance asks whether there's a standard invoicing net-30 and if purchase orders accepted?
[06:02] Samira: Yes, net-30 standard, we accept POs for enterprise deals. We'll ensure billing terms are in the MSA.
[06:09] Priya: For the DPA tangent — can Redwood support data deletion on request and certify deletion including backups?
[06:18] Ethan: Yes, we support data deletion requests; for hosted we run a deletion workflow and can provide a compliance certificate. Backups are handled per retention policy; we'll document the process.
[06:31] Laura: Are penetration tests allowed? Our security team will want to run an external pen test or at least a review of the infra config.
[06:40] Ethan: We can coordinate; usually pen tests are allowed with a notice and scope defined. We'll share the process.
[06:49] Michael: Any red flags from Redwood's side — are there any commercial term items you want to call out?
[06:55] Samira: Nothing unusual; main things are liability cap, data residency specifics, KMS arrangement — those are typical negotiation points.
[07:05] Jamal: For the canary rollout, how do you handle fallback if a new model regresses?
[07:12] Ethan: We support automatic fallback policies and A/B rollouts with traffic splitting; also quality monitoring tied to prompt sets so we can alert on regressions.
[07:23] Priya: Can you point to the SOC2 report and ISO certs? We need the latest reports for our vendor due diligence.
[07:29] Samira: I'll share the security pack link — SOC2 Type II and ISO certs are in there. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/aurum (shared after call).
[07:41] Michael: Sounds good. Procurement notes: we need the final price + versioned contract for review by Friday EOD to hit our two-week target.
[07:51] Samira: We'll aim for redlines back by Monday morning and final pricing spreadsheet by Tuesday.
[07:58] Jamal: One last technical: our workload has a lot of small low-latency calls and some batch embedding jobs — will caching/batching options be configurable per route?
[08:09] Ethan: Yes, we recommend route-based configs: different batching strategies, prefix caching, and KV cache tuning per model. We'll include suggestions in the runbook.
[08:22] Priya: Anything about export controls or restricted data?
[08:26] Samira: If you have restricted datasets we can discuss private deployment / on-premetics — we'll include options.
[08:33] Michael: Ok let's recap and list next steps.
[08:37] Samira: Recap: Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA (Samira), security pack and SOC2 (Samira), benchmark and onboarding runbook (Ethan). Aurum to confirm procurement path and PO time, provide any final legal redlines.
[08:55] Priya: We'll get legal comments back by 05/29.
[08:58] Samira: Great. Thanks everyone.
[09:00] Laura: Thanks.
[09:02] Meeting end.
